implementation_summary: accessibilityBasics(page, { urlPath, ids, testCaseId?, role? }) calls UXQualityChecker.check at breakpoint '1440px' with enableAxe true. The tap-target rule only runs at 375px, so it never fires here. Only axe violations are kept: ids starting with F-A11Y-, minus F-A11Y-REVIEW- and F-A11Y-SCAN-FAILED-. Each one becomes an AuditFinding with id = ids.next() (AF-NNN), rule = the axe rule id parsed from the trailing '(rule-id)' of the checker title, group 'technical', area 'accessibility', source 'checker', sectionId null, severity and findingId kept, target = cssSelector, and detail 'On <urlPath>: <checker actual>'. Impact comes from severity (Blocker/Major high, Minor medium, Suggestion low); effort is 'low'. Basics = { standard 'WCAG 2.2', level 'AA', method 'automatic checks only', violations = number of mapped findings, findingIds = their AF ids }. If check() throws or returns an F-A11Y-SCAN-FAILED finding, the result is basics null, findings [] and the note 'The accessibility checks did not run on <path>, so this page has not been checked.' No ids are used up in that case. axe's own text can contain ADR 0018 words: on the gallery page, the target-size summary says 'Safe clickable space'. So title, detail and suggestion go through withoutClaimWords (uses findClaimWords from documents/wording.ts), which drops any sentence or line containing a claim word and falls back to neutral text if nothing is left. packages/checkers is unchanged.
